result.title: BehaviorICL: Task-Conditioned Decoder States for Visual In-Context Learning
result.summary: The usefulness of an in-context demonstration for a vision-language model (VLM) depends on both the query image and the task posed about it. We study whether the frozen target VLM's own decoder states, read before answer generation, can select such demonstrations. BehaviorICL represents each image and task by a task-conditioned processing signature, the hidden states at the final input position across all decoder layers. Its training-free variant, BehaviorICL-Raw, averages cosine similarities between corresponding layer states and passes the retrieved examples with their reference answers to the same VLM. When the same NICO++ images are asked about their object or their context, Raw retrieves largely different demonstrations for the two questions and outperforms an image retriever given task-matched demonstrations on both VLMs. Across two VLMs and eight classification and visual question answering datasets, Raw gives the highest average accuracy among training-free retrievers on both VLMs and exceeds RICES with a CLIP ViT-L/14 encoder by 3.83 points on Qwen and 1.85 on InternVL. A lightweight shared projection, BehaviorICL-Proj, brings further gains on classification. Analyses of extraction text, decoder depth and bank answers help explain these gains, and attention analysis describes how the task text shifts attention at the extraction position toward the classified object. These results support the target VLM's internal states as a practical basis for visual in-context learning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BehaviorICL：把冻结 VLM 在答案生成前、最后一个输入位置跨所有 decoder 层的隐藏状态作为任务条件化的「处理签名」，据此检索上下文示例；给出免训练的逐层余弦相似度平均（Raw）与轻量共享投影（Proj）两种变体，并在两个 VLM、八个分类与 VQA 数据集上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及「内部状态是否保留任务必要视觉信息」这一问题——同一图像问物体或问语境时检索结果明显不同；其关于 decoder 深度、提取位置文本和注意力偏移的分析，可供核查 latent 相似度中内容、深度与位置因素的影响，但该状态用于示例检索而非推理期 latent 生成。
